# Clojure language fixture

The CLI asks the service to compose a greeting and write it to a named file.
The JVM branch of the shared source reads the clock. A function parameter is
called independently of a similarly named global, and a call written in a
macro's argument keeps its own caller. The tests import clojure.test, and the
`:test` alias runs the whole `test` directory, its shared rows included.
A Quil sketch and a websocket are handed the repository's functions under
keywords, and a future starts a greeting on its own thread. The shadow-cljs
`:app` build is a browser page of its own, started from `example.web/init`.
These examples exercise the ordinary clj-kondo → ProgramIndex adapter.
